description: Footnote label / marker grammars extracted VERBATIM from engine legalpdf/core.py (the PDF footnote-linking pass). Spelling follows the sources exactly: superscript digits, † ‡ § ¶ and ⟦ ⟧ are literal where the source writes them literally (_LABEL_RE/_PURE_LABEL_RE/_SUPER_RE/_INLINE_FN_RE), while _STANDALONE_REF_RE's \u2020\u2021\u00a7\u00b6 escapes and _DOUBLE_ZERO_WIDTH_RE's invisible \u200b are kept as escapes exactly as the source spells them — a spelling dialect, not a semantic one. (?P<label> translated to JS syntax. Python compiles re.ASCII, JS without u. None of these carry re.I.

entries.provenance: engine core.py:33-35 (_LABEL_RE; (?P<label> translated to JS syntax, symbols literal in source). A footnote label at line start: 1-4 digits or a mark, then whitespace or closing punctuation. CanLII-style [N] bracket numbering does not match.

vectors.input: 38 Representation before a tribunal concerns legal rights.
* The author thanks the anonymous reviewers

entries.provenance: engine core.py:36 (_PURE_LABEL_RE, symbols literal in source). The whole string IS the label — no trailing punctuation, unlike label.line-start.
engine core.py:38 (_SUPER_RE). Superscript digits stay literal, as in the source; core.py:37 pairs this with _SUPER_TRANSLATION to map them to ASCII digits.

engine core.py:39-41 (_SENTENCE_EDGE_RE). The ENGINE DIALECT of boundary.sentence.splitter (references.json): instead of looking forward to the next sentence's opener+capital, it consumes trailing closers (" ' ” ’ ) ]) after the terminal punctuation and requires whitespace, a ⟦FN: marker, or end-of-text next. Source spells the straight quote \"; written literal (compiled-identical); ” ’ ⟦ literal in source.

criminal liability. Depriving a person of liberty
R v X, 2020 SCC 1 at para.20

entries.provenance: engine core.py:42 (_INLINE_FN_RE) == adapters.py:99 (inline re.sub copy, byte-identical pattern). The engine's internal footnote-reference marker; ⟦ U+27E6 / ⟧ U+27E7 literal in both sources. Requires a non-empty id.

entries.provenance: engine core.py:50 (_STANDALONE_REF_RE). Same token shape as label.pure but unanchored (used against isolated reference-mark spans). The SOURCE spells † ‡ § ¶ as \u2020\u2021\u00a7\u00b6 escapes here (unlike _LABEL_RE's literals); kept exactly — the compiled characters are identical.

entries.provenance: engine core.py:51 (_DOUBLE_ZERO_WIDTH_RE). Two or more consecutive zero-width spaces — an extraction-defect tripwire. Invisible character stays a \u200b escape, per the authoring rule and the source's own spelling. Vector inputs carry real U+200B characters (JSON-escaped for visibility).
